title: Accountability Ledger Event Contract
description: Machine-checkable form of ONE line in the hash-chained, append-only ACCOUNTABILITY LEDGER (Phase 0.2 — .tess/state/ledger/<YYYY-MM>.<origin>.jsonl). The 'who did what, when, who's holding it' audit trail Xavier's re-aimed vision calls for, sibling to task.schema.json (which tracks the CURRENT state of a task; this schema tracks the immutable HISTORY of events that produced it). Ported from Hermes' kanban design's task_events audit (kb/wiki/synthesis/2026-07-19-hermes-codebase-fork-study.md). `tessctl log append` dogfood-validates every event against THIS schema (via the in-memory dict, before it is ever written to a shard — `_ledger_self_validate_or_raise`) — same discipline as `_self_validate_or_raise` for mission/task records, adapted to a value that is appended rather than a file that is replaced. Each shard's own hash chain is independently tamper-evident (`tessctl log verify`): `hash = sha256(prev_hash + canonical_json(event minus hash))`, `prev_hash` of the first event in a shard is 64 zero hex chars (genesis).

ts.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp ('...Z' suffix) this event was appended — NOT necessarily when the underlying action started (e.g. a `claim` event's `ts` is append time; the task record's own `claim.claimed_at` is the authoritative claim-start time).

actor.description: Who/what produced this event — the cross-harness accountability identity: which harness, optionally which model/session/persona.

event.description: Event classification. `task_transition` covers any tracked change to a task record via `tessctl tasks new|set` (including creation itself, logged as '(none) -> <initial status>'); `claim`/`heartbeat`/`release`/`completed`/`crashed`/`reclaimed` are `tessctl tasks claim|release`'s own five-way claim-lifecycle classification (Hermes' 'claimed/completed/crashed/reclaimed' vocabulary, verbatim); `dispatch`/`session_open`/`session_close` are broader harness-lifecycle bookkeeping events logged directly via `tessctl log append`, not tied to any one task.

refs.description: What this event refers to. `_lint_ledger_event` requires `refs.task` to be non-null for every task-scoped event class (`task_transition`, `claim`, `heartbeat`, `release`, `completed`, `crashed`, `reclaimed`) — a relational rule plain JSON Schema cannot express against a sibling field's own value.

summary.description: Human-readable one-line description of what happened (e.g. 'status: backlog -> in_progress', 'claimed by ada-host:4821:9c1e...'). Never empty — an empty summary carries no accountability information, the same rule task.schema.json's Note.text already applies.

prev_hash.description: The `hash` of the immediately preceding event IN THIS SAME SHARD (64 zero hex chars — genesis — for the first event ever appended to a shard). Chains are per-shard, NOT global: shards are sharded per calendar month AND per writer origin specifically so two machines/harnesses writing concurrently never contend on, or need to interleave into, the SAME chain (see .tess/bin/tessctl's TASK LEDGER region header).

hash.description: sha256(`prev_hash` + compact key-sorted JSON of this event with the `hash` key itself removed) — the same 'canonical bytes minus the field being computed' construction `verdict_canonical_bytes`/`signoff_canonical_bytes` already use elsewhere in this engine, applied here to a hash chain instead of a signature. `tessctl log verify` recomputes this for every line and compares; any mismatch, OR any `prev_hash` that does not equal the prior line's `hash`, is reported as tamper.

model.description: Which model was driving the harness, if known/relevant.

session.description: The harness session id, if the caller supplied one.

persona.description: Which named persona/agent (e.g. 'Ada') was acting, if relevant.

task.description: Task id this event refers to, or null for a task-independent event (dispatch/session_open/session_close).

mission.description: Mission id this event refers to, or null.

$comment: Minimal-validator keyword subset supported by tessctl validate: type, enum, const, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, minItems, maxItems, minLength, maxLength, pattern, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, if/then/else, oneOf, anyOf, allOf, contains, $ref, $defs.
